items.title: KVS is an autonomous body under MoE
items.body: Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) is an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Education, Government of India. It runs Kendriya Vidyalayas across the country. Always treat the latest recruitment notification on the official site as the source of truth for a given cycle.

items.title: PRT means Primary Teacher
items.body: PRT in KVS recruitment refers to Primary Teacher posts, typically associated with primary classes. Exact class range, pay level, and subject combination for a vacancy are stated in that cycle's official notification, not in unofficial Telegram forwards.

items.title: Use the official KVS website for notifications
items.body: Recruitment advertisements, application windows, admit cards, and result notices are published through official KVS / Government of India channels (notably kvsangathan.nic.in). Do not treat coaching-site summaries as final eligibility or document lists.

items.title: Eligibility and age relaxation are notification-specific
items.body: Age limits, educational qualifications, CTET/TET requirements, and category-wise age relaxation (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ex-servicemen) follow the Government of India rules as written in the specific KVS recruitment notification. Do not memorise a number from a previous year as if it still applies.

items.title: Document verification is part of selection
items.body: KVS teaching recruitment typically includes verification of original certificates (education, category, TET/CTET where required, identity, and experience if claimed). Carry originals plus photocopies and photo ID as listed on the interview/document-verification call letter for that cycle.

items.title: Rely on the call letter, not hearsay
items.body: Venue, reporting time, documents, and whether a teaching demonstration is required are specified on the official interview/document verification call letter. If a coaching note conflicts with the call letter, the call letter wins.

items.title: Panel commonly probes pedagogy with classroom examples
items.body: KVS PRT interviews historically emphasise Child Development and Pedagogy: how you would teach a concept, handle mixed-ability learners, and keep a primary classroom inclusive. Answers should include a concrete classroom example, not only theory names.

items.title: Teaching demonstration is often expected
items.body: Many KVS teaching interviews include or are followed by a short teaching demonstration. Prepare a 5–8 minute primary lesson with a learning outcome, one activity, and a quick check for understanding. Keep language simple and child-centred.

items.title: Interview language can be English or Hindi
items.body: Candidates may be asked questions in English, Hindi, or a mix, depending on the panel. Clarity and a classroom example matter more than ornate vocabulary. If you switch languages, stay consistent within an answer.

items.title: Previous cycles mixed written exam and interview
items.body: Recent KVS teaching recruitments have often combined a computer-based written exam with a later interview / document verification stage. Weightage between written and interview, if any, is defined only in that cycle's notification. Do not assume last year's ratio still applies.

items.title: Classroom management questions repeat across years
items.body: Candidates from previous cycles commonly report questions on slow learners, large class sizes, inclusive education, and how you would start a lesson in EVS, language, or primary maths. Treat these as practice themes, not leaked papers.

items.title: Common theme: slow learner in a large class
items.body: A frequent PRT interview prompt is: how will you support a child who is struggling while the rest of the class moves ahead? A grounded answer names diagnosis (what the child cannot yet do), a simple scaffold, peer support, and how you still protect the child's dignity.

items.title: Common theme: NEP 2020 in a primary classroom
items.body: Panels often ask how NEP 2020 ideas show up in Class 1–5: foundational literacy and numeracy, competency-based tasks, mother-tongue comfort, and reduced rote. Answer with one activity you would actually run, not a list of policy slogans.

items.title: Common theme: inclusive education
items.body: Expect questions on children with disabilities, multilingual classrooms, and gender-sensitive grouping. A strong answer names one adjustment (seating, extra time, visual support, buddy system) and how you check that it worked.

items.title: Subject knowledge is taught through pedagogy
items.body: For PRT, EVS, language, and maths questions are usually asked as 'how would you teach this to Class 3?' rather than as pure content quizzes. Prepare one demo each for a language poem, an EVS local-environment topic, and a primary maths concept with concrete objects.

items.title: Arrive early with printed papers and photo ID
items.body: On interview day, reach the venue early with the printed call letter, photo identity proof, photographs as specified, and the document file listed in the instructions. Keep a simple water bottle and avoid last-minute certificate printouts at a cyber cafe.
